function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

p = sqlparse.parse('SELECT NULL AS foo')[0]
stmt_tokens = [t for t in p.tokens]
print('Test NULL AS foo tokens:')
for t in p.flatten():
    pass
ident = None
for t in p.tokens:
    if isinstance(t, sql.Identifier):
        ident = t
print('Found Identifier:', ident)
if ident:
    print('get_real_name:', ident.get_real_name())
    print('get_alias:', ident.get_alias())

print()
# Test 2: keyword used as alias target shouldn't be grouped (e.g. SELECT x AS SELECT -- invalid, use a keyword before AS)
p2 = sqlparse.parse('SELECT CASE WHEN 1=1 THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS foo')[0]
for t in p2.tokens:
    if isinstance(t, sql.Identifier):
        print('Case AS Identifier:', t, t.get_alias())

print()
# Test 3: dont alias keywords - keyword before AS shouldn't form identifier
p3 = sqlparse.parse('UPDATE foo SET bar = 1 AS baz')[0]
print([t for t in p3.tokens])

   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+

   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).

   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.

    print('get_alias:', ident.get_alias())

print()

        print('Case AS Identifier:', t, t.get_alias())

print()

print([t for t in p3.tokens])

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

The `valid_prev` check used `token.normalized != 'NULL' or not token.is_keyword`, which for a NULL keyword token evaluates to `False or False == False`, so `NULL AS foo` was incorrectly refused grouping into an Identifier (breaking the 'null with as' behavior), while the original intent (per CHANGELOG: "Fix handling of NULL keywords in aliased identifiers") was that NULL should be treated as a special exception allowed before AS, while other keywords should still be excluded (the 'dont alias keywords' behavior).

structured_output.content:
Investigated the regression in sqlparse's `group_as` function in `sqlparse/engine/grouping.py`. The `valid_prev` check used `token.normalized != 'NULL' or not token.is_keyword`, which for a NULL keyword token evaluates to `False or False == False`, so `NULL AS foo` was incorrectly refused grouping into an Identifier (breaking the 'null with as' behavior), while the original intent (per CHANGELOG: "Fix handling of NULL keywords in aliased identifiers") was that NULL should be treated as a special exception allowed before AS, while other keywords should still be excluded (the 'dont alias keywords' behavior).

I fixed the logic to: `not token.is_keyword or token.normalized == 'NULL'`, which:
- Returns True for any non-keyword token (normal identifiers, functions, etc.) — preserves existing correct behavior.
- Returns True specifically for the NULL keyword — restores `NULL AS foo` grouping into an Identifier with real_name/alias 'foo'.
- Returns False for any other keyword (TRUE, FALSE, ASC, DISTINCT, etc.) before AS — preserves 'dont alias keywords' behavior (keywords aren't merged into the Identifier via AS).

Verified via ad-hoc script:
- `SELECT NULL AS foo` → grouped as Identifier 'NULL AS foo', get_real_name()=='foo', get_alias()=='foo' (previously failed to group).
- `SELECT TRUE AS flag` / `SELECT FALSE AS flag` / `SELECT ASC AS x` / `SELECT DISTINCT AS x` → NOT grouped with the preceding keyword (only 'flag'/'x' identifier remains), i.e. keywords are not aliased via AS — matches 'dont alias keywords'.
- Normal cases (`foo AS bar`, `MAX(x) AS mx`, CASE...AS foo, lists) continue to work correctly.

This single, minimal, targeted fix in grouping.py restores both previously-passing behaviors without affecting other grouping logic.

Investigated the regression in sqlparse's `group_as` function in `sqlparse/engine/grouping.py`. The `valid_prev` check used `token.normalized != 'NULL' or not token.is_keyword`, which for a NULL keyword token evaluates to `False or False == False`, so `NULL AS foo` was incorrectly refused grouping into an Identifier (breaking the 'null with as' behavior), while the original intent (per CHANGELOG: "Fix handling of NULL keywords in aliased identifiers") was that NULL should be treated as a special exception allowed before AS, while other keywords should still be excluded (the 'dont alias keywords' behavior).

I fixed the logic to: `not token.is_keyword or token.normalized == 'NULL'`, which:
- Returns True for any non-keyword token (normal identifiers, functions, etc.) — preserves existing correct behavior.
- Returns True specifically for the NULL keyword — restores `NULL AS foo` grouping into an Identifier with real_name/alias 'foo'.
- Returns False for any other keyword (TRUE, FALSE, ASC, DISTINCT, etc.) before AS — preserves 'dont alias keywords' behavior (keywords aren't merged into the Identifier via AS).

Verified via ad-hoc script:
- `SELECT NULL AS foo` → grouped as Identifier 'NULL AS foo', get_real_name()=='foo', get_alias()=='foo' (previously failed to group).
- `SELECT TRUE AS flag` / `SELECT FALSE AS flag` / `SELECT ASC AS x` / `SELECT DISTINCT AS x` → NOT grouped with the preceding keyword (only 'flag'/'x' identifier remains), i.e. keywords are not aliased via AS — matches 'dont alias keywords'.
- Normal cases (`foo AS bar`, `MAX(x) AS mx`, CASE...AS foo, lists) continue to work correctly.

This single, minimal, targeted fix in grouping.py restores both previously-passing behaviors without affecting other grouping logic.

Investigated the regression in sqlparse's `group_as` function in `sqlparse/engine/grouping.py`. The `valid_prev` check used `token.normalized != 'NULL' or not token.is_keyword`, which for a NULL keyword token evaluates to `False or False == False`, so `NULL AS foo` was incorrectly refused grouping into an Identifier (breaking the 'null with as' behavior), while the original intent (per CHANGELOG: "Fix handling of NULL keywords in aliased identifiers") was that NULL should be treated as a special exception allowed before AS, while other keywords should still be excluded (the 'dont alias keywords' behavior).

I fixed the logic to: `not token.is_keyword or token.normalized == 'NULL'`, which:
- Returns True for any non-keyword token (normal identifiers, functions, etc.) — preserves existing correct behavior.
- Returns True specifically for the NULL keyword — restores `NULL AS foo` grouping into an Identifier with real_name/alias 'foo'.
- Returns False for any other keyword (TRUE, FALSE, ASC, DISTINCT, etc.) before AS — preserves 'dont alias keywords' behavior (keywords aren't merged into the Identifier via AS).

Verified via ad-hoc script:
- `SELECT NULL AS foo` → grouped as Identifier 'NULL AS foo', get_real_name()=='foo', get_alias()=='foo' (previously failed to group).
- `SELECT TRUE AS flag` / `SELECT FALSE AS flag` / `SELECT ASC AS x` / `SELECT DISTINCT AS x` → NOT grouped with the preceding keyword (only 'flag'/'x' identifier remains), i.e. keywords are not aliased via AS — matches 'dont alias keywords'.
- Normal cases (`foo AS bar`, `MAX(x) AS mx`, CASE...AS foo, lists) continue to work correctly.

This single, minimal, targeted fix in grouping.py restores both previously-passing behaviors without affecting other grouping logic.

   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.

Investigated the regression in sqlparse's `group_as` function in `sqlparse/engine/grouping.py`. The `valid_prev` check used `token.normalized != 'NULL' or not token.is_keyword`, which for a NULL keyword token evaluates to `False or False == False`, so `NULL AS foo` was incorrectly refused grouping into an Identifier (breaking the 'null with as' behavior), while the original intent (per CHANGELOG: "Fix handling of NULL keywords in aliased identifiers") was that NULL should be treated as a special exception allowed before AS, while other keywords should still be excluded (the 'dont alias keywords' behavior).

I fixed the logic to: `not token.is_keyword or token.normalized == 'NULL'`, which:
- Returns True for any non-keyword token (normal identifiers, functions, etc.) — preserves existing correct behavior.
- Returns True specifically for the NULL keyword — restores `NULL AS foo` grouping into an Identifier with real_name/alias 'foo'.
- Returns False for any other keyword (TRUE, FALSE, ASC, DISTINCT, etc.) before AS — preserves 'dont alias keywords' behavior (keywords aren't merged into the Identifier via AS).

Verified via ad-hoc script:
- `SELECT NULL AS foo` → grouped as Identifier 'NULL AS foo', get_real_name()=='foo', get_alias()=='foo' (previously failed to group).
- `SELECT TRUE AS flag` / `SELECT FALSE AS flag` / `SELECT ASC AS x` / `SELECT DISTINCT AS x` → NOT grouped with the preceding keyword (only 'flag'/'x' identifier remains), i.e. keywords are not aliased via AS — matches 'dont alias keywords'.
- Normal cases (`foo AS bar`, `MAX(x) AS mx`, CASE...AS foo, lists) continue to work correctly.

This single, minimal, targeted fix in grouping.py restores both previously-passing behaviors without affecting other grouping logic.

   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:

   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+

   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).

   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.

Investigated the regression in sqlparse's `group_as` function in `sqlparse/engine/grouping.py`. The `valid_prev` check used `token.normalized != 'NULL' or not token.is_keyword`, which for a NULL keyword token evaluates to `False or False == False`, so `NULL AS foo` was incorrectly refused grouping into an Identifier (breaking the 'null with as' behavior), while the original intent (per CHANGELOG: "Fix handling of NULL keywords in aliased identifiers") was that NULL should be treated as a special exception allowed before AS, while other keywords should still be excluded (the 'dont alias keywords' behavior).

I fixed the logic to: `not token.is_keyword or token.normalized == 'NULL'`, which:
- Returns True for any non-keyword token (normal identifiers, functions, etc.) — preserves existing correct behavior.
- Returns True specifically for the NULL keyword — restores `NULL AS foo` grouping into an Identifier with real_name/alias 'foo'.
- Returns False for any other keyword (TRUE, FALSE, ASC, DISTINCT, etc.) before AS — preserves 'dont alias keywords' behavior (keywords aren't merged into the Identifier via AS).

Verified via ad-hoc script:
- `SELECT NULL AS foo` → grouped as Identifier 'NULL AS foo', get_real_name()=='foo', get_alias()=='foo' (previously failed to group).
- `SELECT TRUE AS flag` / `SELECT FALSE AS flag` / `SELECT ASC AS x` / `SELECT DISTINCT AS x` → NOT grouped with the preceding keyword (only 'flag'/'x' identifier remains), i.e. keywords are not aliased via AS — matches 'dont alias keywords'.
- Normal cases (`foo AS bar`, `MAX(x) AS mx`, CASE...AS foo, lists) continue to work correctly.

This single, minimal, targeted fix in grouping.py restores both previously-passing behaviors without affecting other grouping logic.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

structured_output.content:
The fix has been applied and verified. Since the repository doesn't ship a `tests/` directory in this checkout (hidden tests will be supplied separately), I validated the fix manually against representative SQL inputs covering both reported regressions:

- 'null with as': `SELECT NULL AS foo` now correctly groups into an `Identifier` with `get_real_name() == 'foo'` and `get_alias() == 'foo'` (previously failed to group at all).
- 'dont alias keywords': `SELECT TRUE AS flag`, `SELECT ASC AS x`, `SELECT DISTINCT AS x` etc. still correctly refuse to merge the keyword into the aliased identifier (only the alias name remains as the Identifier).
- Regression-free on existing correct behavior: `foo AS bar`, `MAX(x) AS mx`, CASE...AS foo, IdentifierLists, etc. still work as before.

The single-line fix is in `sqlparse/engine/grouping.py`, `group_as()`'s `valid_prev` predicate, changed from the buggy `token.normalized != 'NULL' or not token.is_keyword` (which evaluated to False for the NULL keyword, breaking the NULL-AS-alias case) to `not token.is_keyword or token.normalized == 'NULL'` (which correctly treats NULL as a special-cased keyword allowed before AS, while still rejecting other keywords from being treated as aliasable targets).

I attempted to run the test suite via `pytest -q` but this checkout has no `tests/` directory present (glob and pytest both report none), so hidden upstream tests will supply the actual check. No further local test files were added per instructions.

arguments.summary: Fixed regression in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_as() valid_prev predicate. The previous logic `token.normalized != 'NULL' or not token.is_keyword` incorrectly evaluated to False when the previous token was the NULL keyword, preventing `NULL AS alias` from being grouped into an Identifier (breaking the 'null with as' behavior). Changed to `not token.is_keyword or token.normalized == 'NULL'`, which allows NULL specifically to precede AS and form an aliased Identifier (restoring 'null with as'), while still correctly rejecting other keywords (TRUE, FALSE, ASC, DISTINCT, etc.) from being merged into an aliased Identifier via AS (preserving 'dont alias keywords'). Verified manually with sqlparse.parse() on representative SQL: NULL AS foo, foo AS NULL, TRUE/FALSE/ASC/DISTINCT AS x, foo AS bar, MAX(x) AS mx, CASE...AS foo, and multi-identifier lists — all behave correctly post-fix with no other regressions observed.

message.content:
The fix has been applied and verified. Since the repository doesn't ship a `tests/` directory in this checkout (hidden tests will be supplied separately), I validated the fix manually against representative SQL inputs covering both reported regressions:

- 'null with as': `SELECT NULL AS foo` now correctly groups into an `Identifier` with `get_real_name() == 'foo'` and `get_alias() == 'foo'` (previously failed to group at all).
- 'dont alias keywords': `SELECT TRUE AS flag`, `SELECT ASC AS x`, `SELECT DISTINCT AS x` etc. still correctly refuse to merge the keyword into the aliased identifier (only the alias name remains as the Identifier).
- Regression-free on existing correct behavior: `foo AS bar`, `MAX(x) AS mx`, CASE...AS foo, IdentifierLists, etc. still work as before.

The single-line fix is in `sqlparse/engine/grouping.py`, `group_as()`'s `valid_prev` predicate, changed from the buggy `token.normalized != 'NULL' or not token.is_keyword` (which evaluated to False for the NULL keyword, breaking the NULL-AS-alias case) to `not token.is_keyword or token.normalized == 'NULL'` (which correctly treats NULL as a special-cased keyword allowed before AS, while still rejecting other keywords from being treated as aliasable targets).

I attempted to run the test suite via `pytest -q` but this checkout has no `tests/` directory present (glob and pytest both report none), so hidden upstream tests will supply the actual check. No further local test files were added per instructions.

function.name: finish
function.arguments: {"summary": "Fixed regression in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_as() valid_prev predicate. The previous logic `token.normalized != 'NULL' or not token.is_keyword` incorrectly evaluated to False when the previous token was the NULL keyword, preventing `NULL AS alias` from being grouped into an Identifier (breaking the 'null with as' behavior). Changed to `not token.is_keyword or token.normalized == 'NULL'`, which allows NULL specifically to precede AS and form an aliased Identifier (restoring 'null with as'), while still correctly rejecting other keywords (TRUE, FALSE, ASC, DISTINCT, etc.) from being merged into an aliased Identifier via AS (preserving 'dont alias keywords'). Verified manually with sqlparse.parse() on representative SQL: NULL AS foo, foo AS NULL, TRUE/FALSE/ASC/DISTINCT AS x, foo AS bar, MAX(x) AS mx, CASE...AS foo, and multi-identifier lists — all behave correctly post-fix with no other regressions observed."}
